text:
Alex: Heads-up — noticed steady KV memory growth on prod longctx runs. 3 tenants show residency creeping up over 48h, not reclaiming.
Maria: Which tenants? any noisy traffic patterns?
Alex: tenant-a, tenant-c, tenant-e. tenant-a steady token-per-minute surge, tenant-e bursty but keeps slabs pinned.
Sam: Can you paste the longtail pmap/ps output? wondering if it's fragmentation vs pinned pages.
Alex: pasted initial snapshot from one host: 
```
RSS: 62G
AnonHugePages: 0
Mapped: 8G
Slab: 12G
kv-residency: 38G (pages pinned by alloc slabs)
```
I think slab reuse is failing for longctx allocations; pages aren't being returned to freelist.
Irene: That matches a repro I ran — longctx sequences with streaming cache hit patterns leave partial-page fragments that never merge. We saw bump in slab-frag metrics + low compaction triggers.
Maria: Any recent kernel or jemalloc changes?
Sam: No kernel bump in prod last 2 weeks. We did push a batching heuristic tweak and a KV pinning optimization in runtime v1.43. Might be related.
perf-bot: New perf trace generated: https://perf.internal/traces/3659871234/kv-slab-ratcheting — includes heapshot + pprof.
Alex: From pprof flame: heavy time in slab allocator free path, but free path no-ops because reference counts remain >0. Suspect lease-window ratcheting keeps refs.
Irene: The lease-window logic increments a tenant lease on every background touch; with longctx we end up ratcheting the LRU timestamp so eviction never sees them as cold.
Maria: So noisy tenant keeps renewing pages by walking KV for long sequences => effectively pins.
Sam: Proposal: add a decay check for longctx read-only walks: if page hit frequency > X and last-write > Y, don't bump residency timestamp. Basically stop ratcheting for read-only streaming hits.
Alex: Agreed. Also add slab compaction job that targets fragmented buckets older than 24h. We can run during low-load windows.
Irene: We should be careful: disabling ratchet might increase tail latency for workloads that genuinely rely on reuse. Need canary and metric watchlist: per-tenant 95p latency, kv-hit-rate, reclamation-rate.
Maria: +1. Also throttle leak-prone tenants with per-tenant residency quotas. If quota exceeded, apply soft-evict and request-level backpressure (429 or degraded model variant).
Sam: I sketched config for soft quota policy: 
```
{"quota_mb": 8192, "grace_seconds": 3600, "throttle_pct": 0.1, "fallback_model": "quant-8g"}
```
Alex: Nice. Let's test in staging: enable decay-flag, run longctx generator for tenant-a/c/e patterns, measure resident pages and compaction events.
perf-bot: Staging job queued: job/kv-ratcheting-check-365987. Will post results.
Irene: Also add a tiny telemetry change: emit "ratchet_event" for read-only hits so we can measure how often ratcheting occurs per tenant.
Maria: Action items: 
- Alex: run staging experiment and attach heapshots (due EOD)
- Sam: implement decay toggle + soft-quota enforcement in runtime (PR draft)
- Irene: instrument ratchet_event and slab-frag eviction metric
- Maria: prepare canary rollout plan & alert thresholds
Alex: I'll also capture a pprof before/after for the free path.
Sam: I'll open the draft PR and link here.
Alex: Thanks — if staging shows reclamation, we can canary to a small prod ring tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Maria: If noisy tenants keep pinning after that, we may need stronger penalties (hard quota or tenant routing to dedicated pool). Keep everyone looped.
perf-bot: Tracking tag: #kv-ratcheting-365987
